chunks.text: Next we will talk about a very important concept which is called binary search
Binary search is a concept that is asked in many interviews and coding tests
Here we will tell you what is binary search
If you have seen dictionaries, then there is a very big dictionary
If we want to find the meaning of the word mango, then we will do a linear search
We will not do it like this, because dictionaries are sorted
In the beginning, it will be written as apple, banana, chiku, lychee, mango and strawberry
In such cases, when we know how things are written in the dictionary
We know that M is bigger than A, M is bigger than B
We will try to search these things
We know that mango will not come in the last or in the beginning of the dictionary
It will be somewhere in the middle
And then we see where it is sorted in which order
Let's put an idea, then we find mango in the dictionary
There is a similar concept of binary search
It is not the same concept, it is the same concept of binary search
Binary search is always on a sorted array
The prerequisite thing for this is a sorted array
Either the array is in increasing order 5, 6, 7
Or the array is in decreasing order 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3
Now if we want to find a key in this array
We will find out whether it should come on the left or right side
Now if we take the example of the above array
Suppose we want to find 2 in this array
We will know that it will not exist in this area
Because there are big numbers here
It will exist somewhere in the beginning
This is the logic of binary search
Now let's see how binary search actually happens
We have an example of an array in which the elements are stored
The key for which we have to search is key is equal to 10
We have to search for 10
So the simple technique of binary search will be
What do we take in the beginning?
Let's take a start
Our index will be 0 when it starts
Our index will end
How many elements are there in this?
7 elements, so our 7 will end
Now when we have to do comparison in the beginning
We will start from the middle
We will see whether our key exists in the middle of the array
The middle value for this array will be 8
So this is our mid
We will compare mid with key first
If our mid is bigger than the key
Then we will know that if mid is big
Then the one after mid will also be bigger than the key
So there is no chance of getting the key
So what we will do
Then we will search the key in our first half
But if our mid is smaller than the key
So in that case if mid is smaller than the key
Then the one before mid, means these elements will also be smaller than the key
Like here our key is 10
And we have to search, our mid is 8
Now if the element before 8 is sorted
Then it will be even smaller than 8
There will not get the key
So we already know that if our mid is smaller than our key
Means 8 is smaller than our key
Means it is smaller than 10
So now we will search in our second half
So let's write the second half array
In the second half array, 10, 12, and 40 will come
Now here this will be our start
This will be our end
This will be our mid
We will check the same condition again
Is our mid, means 12, our key bigger than 10
Bigger means we will not be able to find it in the elements after that
So we will find it in the first half
We will find the key in the first half
After this, in the first half, there is only 10
Its start is the same, its end is the same, and its mid is also the same
Because it is an array of single element
So here we will compare the key
We will get the key
What is the key? Key is equal to 10
Our mid is also equal to 10
Means here we will get the match
So what was the process?
We will summarize the process a little
Now if we summarize the binary search a little
So what did we see?
We saw that we have an array
In the array, we have a lot of elements stored in sorted format
Now here first of all we will calculate the start and end
Between the starting and ending index, we will first find a mid
With this mid, we will compare that our key is smaller than mid, bigger than mid, or equal to it
If it is equal, then simply return that mid
Because here we got our key
If it is small, then what to do in that case?
If the key is smaller than our mid
So in that case, it will ultimately be smaller than the elements after mid
So we have to search in our first half
And if it becomes big, then we have to search in our second half
So these are our laws coming out of here
Now what to do after this?
Suppose we have to check in the first half
So to check in the first half, the size of our array will be half
After that, this will also start, this will also end
The start of this will logically remain the same
Because the start of the first half will be the same as the start of the array
Now the end of this will be mid-1
Why will it be mid-1?
Because we have checked the mid and all the ones after mid are big
So mid-1 will be the end of this
And we will also be taking out a new mid for this
We will take out a new mid, we will also compare the key with this
Whether it is big, small or equal
Whatever happens, after that our array will be one level less
And this time our array will be smaller
So at every level, we will see that in the first bar, if the size of our array is n
Then in the second bar it will be n by 2
In the third bar it will be n by 4
And how long will this process go?
This process will go till the time we do not have a single element in the last
That is, while being half-half, in our dictionary
When we find anything in the dictionary
So we keep searching till we reach the point
Where we just have to check with a single word
What is this word for which we were searching
So the same technique will be applied, our array will be half-half at every level
Every time we will be calculating the start, end and mid
Now let's write a pseudocode and see
With the pseudocode, things will be clearer
First of all, we will start with start from 0 and end with n-1
Because start is the beginning of the array and end is the end of the array
Now here we have to take n-1 because our comparisons are made with end
So this is a very important point to note in binary search
Then we will put a loop
How long will the loop run?
The loop will be conditioned till our start is less than or equal to end
There comes a point where the start is greater than the end
So in that case, the invalid condition is there
Now first of all we will calculate mid
What is our mid?
Start plus end divided by 2
This is a small formula for calculating mid
After this, we will compare mid with key
If our mid is equal to key, then we have got our key
In that case, we will return it
Either we will print the found or the index
If mid is greater than key, then we will search in the first half
That is, we will search in the left side
If mid is less than key, then we will search in the right side
That is, we will search in the second half
Searching in the left half means that we will update the end
Searching in the right half means that we will update the start
For example, if we take the example of this area
If this is our mid
Then the next end that will come in the first half
We will make the end as mid minus 1
But if we want to search in the second half
Then what will happen for the second half?
This will become our start
And what will be the start?
Mid plus 1
So for the first half, the end is updated
For the second half, the start is updated
We have discussed binary search very logically
Let's write the code for this
If anyone is getting a little confusion
Then before writing the code
You have to see a little explanation in another go
And always when you are doing binary search
You have to imagine a dictionary
How we used to find things in the dictionary in childhood
So let's consider another case here
Where our element does not exist in the array
Suppose this is our array
We are searching 99 which does not exist in this array
So in that case, we will do the same thing
Which we did in the linear search
We will return minus 1
